title: Framework Captivity in Core Entities (The Asymmetric Marriage)
pattern: Core business domain models (entities) are directly annotated with database, HTTP, or serialization framework-specific annotations and macros.
why_bad: The business logic is married to a specific external library. If the database schema changes, or if you decide to switch from a SQL database to a Document database, your core business rules must be recompiled and risk breaking.
detection: Structs inside the domain logic/entities folder containing direct import dependencies and attributes from external O/RM or serialization crates.
counterexample: Standard, language-level attributes (like `#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]`) that have zero external runtime dependency.
fix:
Keep domain entities completely pure. Create separate Database Transfer Objects (DTOs) for the framework and map them to domain entities at the boundary.
```rust
struct User { name: String } // Pure domain entity

#[derive(Queryable)]
struct UserRow { id: i32, name: String } // Database-specific DTO
```
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Architecture* (2017), Chapter 22 ("The Dependency Rule") and Chapter 29 ("Frameworks are Details").
